problem:
Calculate the product ${I}_{2}B$ given that ${I}_{2}$ is the $2\times 2$ identity matrix and
$B=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}].$

examples.knowledge_point: Multiplying a Matrix by the Identity Matrix
examples.problem:
Calculate the product $I_3 B$ given that $I_3$ is the $3 \times 3$ identity matrix and
$[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & -1 \\ 5 & 2 & 7 \\ 0 & 4 & 6\end{aligned}]$
examples.worked_solution:
Any matrix, when multiplied by an identity matrix, remains unchanged (assuming that the multiplication is well defined).

The matrix $I_3$ is a $3 \times 3$ matrix and $B$ is a $3 \times 3$ matrix too. 

Therefore, the multiplication is well defined and 

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & -1 \\ 5 & 2 & 7 \\ 0 & 4 & 6\end{aligned}]
$$
